prompt: On the unit circle, the angle $0^\circ$ lands at the point $(1, 0)$. What is $\sin 0^\circ$?

hints.text: The point is $(1, 0)$, so what is its $y$-coordinate?

explanation: On the unit circle, the point at angle $\theta$ is $(\cos \theta,\ \sin \theta)$, so sine is just the height.
At $0^\circ$ the point is $(1, 0)$, sitting right on the $x$-axis with no height at all.

alternativeExplanations.title: Height above the axis
steps: Think of sine as "how high up am I?"
At $0^\circ$ you have not started climbing yet, so the height is 0.
